Meeting Header
Date: 2026-01-15 11:00 PST | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Samantha Ortiz (Redwood AE), Jun Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Mariner - Head ML Ops), Evan Cole (Mariner - Platform), Marta Ruiz (Mariner - Product)

Summary: Quick recap - pilot has been running for 6 days, cache hit rates improving with prefix cache, but tokens/sec/$ is still above target for peak hours. Customer wants a short tradeoff demo showing dedicated nodes vs hosted burst cost.

--- Auto Summary (may be imperfect) ---
- Cache hit around 42% for prefixes, KV cache hit lower at 18% (likely due to session fragmentation)
- Baseline tokens/sec/$ approximate: 1,150 tokens per dollar with hosted standard model; quantized variant estimates 1,700 tokens per dollar but p95 latency +50ms
- Batching at 50-100ms window improves throughput 30% but increases tail latency to unacceptable levels for checkout journey

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samantha: Alright everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick check-in for Mariner pilot week six, want to focus on econ, the caching signal and next steps. Jun you're on the bench numbers right?
[00:18] Jun: Yep, I ran the overnight runs. Some of the numbers are a bit noisy cause the arrival pattern changed Wed night, but overall we see prefix caching saving about 22% token generation on average, so that's good. KV hits are low.
[00:36] Priya: When you say prefix caching 22% is that tokens saved or latency improvement? I thought it was tokens saved but just confirming.
[00:44] Jun: Right, tokens saved — fewer decode steps. Latency also goes down marginally, p50 down 15ms, p95 barely changed because of cold KV misses.
[00:58] Evan: The weird bit for us is the checkout flow sensitivity; any latency > 120ms starts dropping conversions. So p95 is the main concern, not the mean.
[01:12] Marta: product ask — can we see tokens/sec per dollar breakdown for the two main models we tested? Our PMs want a short slide.
[01:20] Samantha: Absolutely. Current hosted baseline is ~1.15k tokens/$ for the standard fp16-ish model we ran. The quantitative run for q4-quant shows about 1.7k tokens/$ — but note the tail latency increased about 40-60ms on our infra.
[01:40] Priya: 40-60ms on tail — that's quite a bit. Is that because of dequant at runtime or kernel mismatch?
[01:48] Jun: Probably kernel selection and more L2 memory thrash, we're seeing extra copies in the path for that quantized path. Also model variant has a longer decode loop because of different attention kernel which isn't fully optimized yet.
[02:05] Samantha: We also tested batching windows — small window 20-40ms, medium 60-100ms. Medium gave +28-35% throughput but p95 increased to ~180ms in some runs. So it's a tradeoff.
[02:22] Evan: For our use-case, checkout, that p95 is dangerous. So we need either dedicated nodes to tighten that tail or smarter routing: send checkout traffic to hosted low-latency pool and other stuff to dedicated cheaper pool.
[02:38] Jun: Yep, smart routing would do per-route policy: small routing table in console, can pin checkout path to low-latency replicas. That also helps if you want to use a slightly larger model for quality on non-critical flows.
[02:53] Priya: Can Redwood guarantee p95 if we go dedicated capacity? We need an SLA-ish number for procurement.
[03:01] Samantha: For Dedicated we can set an SLO target and allocate nodes to guarantee throughput. We can share a draft SLA but formally that's with the commercial team. 
[03:12] Marta: Also curious about cache fragmentation — Jun said KV hits low. Any quick ideas to increase it?
[03:18] Jun: Two levers: 1) Canonicalize prompts — strip session IDs, reorder stable fields — that raises prefix/KV cache hits a lot. 2) Slightly increase session pinning time so active shoppers keep warm KV. We can provide a small preprocessor snippet to do canonicalization.
[03:34] Priya: We'll try canonicalization on 10% of traffic to measure hit rate increase. Evan will pull logs and share later.
[03:40] Evan: Yep I'll export anonymized traces tonight. Expect to see more duplication in the logs than I thought, so maybe hits will go up to 35-45%.
[03:51] Jun: If hits hit 40% that's roughly another 18-24% tokens saved overall, which materially moves tokens/sec/$ closer to target.
[04:05] Samantha: Great, and about the benchmark Jun — can you run the 12-hour with the q4-quant variant and include kernel-level traces? We want p50, p90, p95, token/sec over time.
[04:17] Jun: I'll kick that off. One note: quantized runs are more sensitive to GPU batch size; I'll include a sweep: batch sizes 1, 2, 4 and batching windows 20, 60, 100ms.
[04:31] Marta: Any idea on cost delta if we go dedicated with 8 GPUs vs hosted burst for our projected 1k rps?
[04:38] Samantha: Preliminary rough numbers — dedicated fully utilized gives a better tokens/$ (approx +40-60%) compared to burst-hosted for steady 24/7 loads. But for spiky 1k rps with big peaks, hosted burst with autoscale might be cheaper unless you get committed discount. I'll put numbers in the pricing sheet.
[04:56] Priya: Sounds good. We will also need to validate SOC2/ISO compliance for Dedicated. We have procurement questions around audit logs and key management.
[05:05] Samantha: Yes, we will attach the security pack — SAML, KMS support, audit logs are available in Private/Dedicated. I'll send the security docs after the call.
[05:14] Evan: On the tokens/sec/$ numbers, can we get a simple CSV comparing: baseline hosted fp16, q4-quant, dedicated fp16, dedicated q4-quant with and without caching? That visual helps finance.
[05:26] Samantha: We'll produce that. Jun will run bench and we'll assemble CSV with columns model, deployment-type, caching-on/off, tokens_per_dollar, p50, p95.
[05:38] Jun: One more data point — we observed that context length distribution in Mariner traces skews short (<=128 tokens) for checkout flows, which favors quantization; longer docs for support chat skew to 512+. That means routing different models per route could be win.
[05:57] Marta: Product also wants an experiment: route support-chat to larger model for better comprehension and checkout to small fast model. If it saves cos while not degrading conversion, big win.
[06:07] Samantha: Totally possible. We'll provide recommended routing rules and a canary plan.
[06:14] Priya: Can we also get rough guidance on caching TTL? Should we set prefix cache TTL to 12h or 1h? We worried about stale info in product text.
[06:23] Jun: For product text that changes fast, keep TTL low (1h). For UI copy and stable prompts, 12h or even 24h is fine. We'll suggest per-route TTL.
[06:33] Samantha: Quick recap and owners — Jun runs bench, Samantha sends pricing and security docs, Evan shares traces, Priya tests canonicalization on 10% traffic, Marta will prepare PM slide for stakeholders.
[06:45] Evan: Quick question — competitor call last week mentioned a 2.2k tokens/$ with a proprietary quant, are we in that ballpark?
[06:53] Jun: Some vendors publish peak numbers that are under idealized workloads. Our 1.7k for q4-quant is realistic for mixed load and includes tail penalties. We can run a tight ideal benchmark if you want to reproduce competitor test conditions.
[07:10] Priya: Let's do realistic numbers for procurement, not marketing ones.
[07:15] Samantha: Agreed. We'll keep the bench conditions aligned to your real traces.
[07:20] Marta: Anything else? If not, we'll wrap.
[07:24] Samantha: No, that's it — we'll follow-up via email with attachments and an invite for the demo. Thanks everyone.
